answer: Each identity is a vertex in the EigenTrust graph; scores derive from normalized, reciprocity-weighted endorsements and transitive trust, then decay by an exponential half-life. Reputation therefore requires sustained honest service, not a brief burst. A freshly spawned sybil has near-zero eigenvector centrality, while colluding accounts cannot amplify one another without trusted incoming paths. As in karst, trust follows established channels; a whisper of fabricated praise cannot meet consensus thresholds.
